central_unknown: Lewis Hamilton's power unit issue from FP2 — if Ferrari need to replace components, Hamilton could take a grid penalty, which would dramatically change his fantasy value by adding overtake potential. Also, the extent of Bortoleto's issues and whether his penalty grows beyond five places.

budget_tiers.core: Antonelli (x2 captain), Leclerc or Verstappen, Ferrari constructor
Antonelli (x2 captain), Hadjar, Red Bull constructor

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Kimi Antonelli
captains.reason: Consensus #1 captain across all channels. ML projects 28.5 exp pts, ppm 1.13, LOW risk, predicted P1→P1. Expected to clinch the F1 Fantasy title and take Driver of the Day (Lance Stroll viral campaign dismissed by FanAmp — FIA has overridden meme votes before). Topped FP1 P2 and FP2 P4, showing strong pace despite limited FP1 running with rookies.

captains.label: Primary
captains.name: Max Verstappen
captains.reason: ML projects 26.6 exp pts, ppm 1.49, MEDIUM risk, predicted P4→P2. Betting lines have him neck-and-neck with Antonelli. FanAmp notes Red Bull may have prioritized race sims in FP2 (hence P5 finish). Strong 2x captain alternative if you believe Red Bull found more pace. BoxBox notes Verstappen's soft tire pace looked promising.

captains.label: Differential
captains.name: Charles Leclerc
captains.reason: ML projects 22.3 exp pts, ppm 1.57 (highest value among top drivers), MEDIUM risk, predicted P2→P3. Topped BOTH practice sessions in Mexico. Austin upgrades clearly working. Was the top-scoring driver in Austin. BoxBox long-run data shows Leclerc had the best race pace on mediums — very consistent 1:21.2s across a long stint. Channels favor him as the primary alternative to Verstappen for the 2x slot.

buy.name: Liam Lawson
buy.note: One of the top midfield drivers per FanAmp. Has a 1-place grid penalty from the Verstappen FP2 incident which could yield an extra overtake point. BoxBox notes his race pace was 'actually not bad.' Needs only 6 points for a budget rise — very doable. Strong B-tier anchor.

buy.name: Gabriel Bortoleto
buy.note: Already confirmed 5-place penalty for new control electronics, could grow larger after FP2 garage time. Had a great recovery drive in Austin scoring double-digit points. Penalty-driven overtake points make him interesting at a low price, though FP2 issues are a concern.

buy.name: Valtteri Bottas
buy.note: Taking all-new power unit components with a 50-place grid drop. At $3M floor price with a brand new PU, he's the safest ultra-budget option. New PU makes him more reliable than other $3M drivers for the remaining races.

consider.name: Isack Hadjar
consider.note: 11 consecutive top-10 finishes. FanAmp says he's still the next-best option if you can't afford a full 4A lineup. However, if budget allows two elite drivers, he becomes a sell. BoxBox long-run data showed him with decent but shorter stints vs Leclerc.

consider.name: Sergio Perez
consider.note: Home race — 300th Grand Prix. Sentimental/crowd favorite. FanAmp includes him in their top lineup for emotional upside. BoxBox considers him as a budget option over Bottas for future value. Not a strong points play but cheap Red Bull exposure.

consider.name: Nico Hulkenberg
consider.note: BoxBox identifies him as having the most budget potential among cheap drivers. Decent midfield option though Audi race pace looked concerning in FP2 data.

consider.name: Lewis Hamilton
consider.note: Parked in FP2 with a suspected PU issue. If he takes an engine penalty, he becomes a high-ceiling recovery play. Without a penalty, he's a strong 4A option — nearly matched Leclerc's race pace in long-run data. Monitor closely through FP3/qualifying.

avoid: Lance Stroll — negative 147 points and 12 DNFs on the season. The viral Driver of the Day campaign will not work (FIA has overridden meme votes before). Do not roster him.
Oscar Piastri — BoxBox explicitly says 'I trust Hadjar a lot more than Piastri' and notes his inconsistent pace. Not worth the premium.
Carlos Sainz — BoxBox skeptical of his value relative to price.
Esteban Ocon — Confirmed OUT for the rest of the race weekend. Remove immediately if rostered.

chips.name: Autopilot
chips.reason: FanAmp suggests this is a good time to use it if you still have it, especially with two strong captain candidates (Antonelli/Verstappen or Antonelli/Leclerc). If one DNFs, auto-swap to the other's 2x could be huge. Even better saved for Brazil where 17 DNFs over last 4 seasons make it extremely valuable.

chips.name: Final Fix
chips.reason: Better saved for Brazil (weather chaos, potential grid penalties) unless Hamilton's PU situation forces a last-minute swap. Brazil has 68% rain chance and historically chaotic qualifying.

chips.name: No Negative
chips.reason: Brazil is the ideal deployment — 17 DNFs over last 4 seasons, high rain probability. F1FantasyPolePosition explicitly says 'smoke them if you got them' for Brazil. Mexico is relatively straightforward by comparison.

chips.name: Wildcard
chips.reason: BoxBox is considering wildcard deployment but leaning toward saving it to set up for the next race weekend. With the triple-header in progress, a wildcard for Brazil or the final races could be more impactful.

watch_items: Lewis Hamilton PU status: If Ferrari replace components, expect a grid penalty — transforms him from standard 4A pick into high-ceiling recovery play with overtake points
Gabriel Bortoleto's penalty size: Currently 5-place for control electronics, but FP2 garage time suggests possible additional components needed — could grow to 10+ places
FP3 Mercedes performance: Russell in P3 during FP2. If he stays top-5 in FP3, Mercedes constructor becomes viable; if he drops, Red Bull constructor gains edge
Lance Stroll Driver of the Day campaign: FIA has historically overridden meme votes (Mazepin 2021, Latifi 2022). Antonelli should still win DOTD — do not adjust lineups for this
Max Verstappen true pace: Only had FP2 (no FP1 due to rookie requirement), may have been sandbagging or doing race sims — FP3 will reveal more
Ocon replacement driver confirmation for remaining races — impacts Haas constructor and budget planning
arc: Mexico is the second race of a triple-header, with Brazil immediately following. The key strategic arc is chip management — Mexico is relatively predictable (Ferrari and Mercedes look strong, Antonelli remains dominant), making it a 'hold your chips' weekend. Brazil's Interlagos presents chaos potential with 55-68% rain probability, historically high DNF rates, and possible grid penalties (Verstappen engine penalty rumors). Channels unanimously agree that defensive chips (Autopilot, Final Fix, No Negative) should be deployed in Brazil rather than Mexico. Budget-wise, picking up Lawson and Bottas now at floor prices positions you for flexibility heading into São Paulo, where the ML projects Antonelli (28.5 exp pts), Verstappen (26.6), and Leclerc (22.3) as the clear top three with Mercedes (61.9 exp pts) and Ferrari (56.1) as the top constructors.
